content.comment_body: Hello everyone, does the [product_name] have retentive marker bits? For example, if you set a marker, will the controller remember its state after the power is turned off and restore it when powered back on? Thanks, [user_name]

Yes, this is possible, but certain conditions need to be met for reliable operation. For example, a basic retentive relay can keep its state closed after a power loss, whereas a relay that depends on a timed input may not maintain its closed state. Could you provide a sample for review?

Hi [user_name], you just need to use a latching relay or a pulse relay. After a power failure, if the 'retentivity' option is enabled, the latching or pulse relay and their output Q will not be reset. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing whether [product_name] can retain output states or marker bits after power loss using retentive or latching features. It is clarified that this functionality is possible by using latching or pulse relays with enabled retentivity, although specific relay types and implementation details influence its reliability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for a straightforward way to have [product_name] remember output or marker states through power failures or system restarts, and expect retentive behavior to be easily set up.
